title: The targeted Entity declares an ownershipField that names no field it actually has
target: AZ7 / depth of the ownership-relation check
why: VALIDATOR-AZ7 item 3 is a CONJUNCTION, and this fixture satisfies the first half while failing the second. First half: the resolved target entity declares an ownershipField — 'Widget' declares 'created_by', a well-formed non-empty string, so the declaration is present and readable. Second half: that value must name a field present in that entity's OWN fields[] — and 'Widget' declares exactly one field, 'label'. Nothing in this manifest is called 'created_by'. The ownership relation is therefore satisfied in form and refers to nothing: it is a pointer with no referent. That is what separates this case from its neighbours, and the separation is the point. az7-n3 fails the FIRST half — the target entity declares no ownershipField at all. az7-n4 also fails the first half on the RESOLVED entity, while a different entity in the manifest declares one that must not be allowed to substitute. Only az7-q2 passes the first half and fails the second, so it is the only case in the set that can tell a validator checking 'declares SOME ownershipField' apart from one checking 'declares an ownershipField THAT RESOLVES'. The end state if it were accepted is az7-n4's end state reached by a different route: an ownership predicate with no column to bind to, over an entity whose rows carry no owner, while 'own' still presents as the narrowest scope in the system. Either the predicate errors at execution — safe only if that error is never swallowed — or the missing field is treated as absent and the predicate is dropped, and 'own' then restricts nothing. Neither outcome may be reached by installation; the manifest is refused instead. One word changed in a published manifest is the whole distance between az7-p1 and this fixture.
notes: VALIDATOR OBLIGATION, NOT A SCHEMA ONE. AUTHORIZATION_STANDARD.md §4.1 VALIDATOR-AZ7 item 3, in full: 'For every Action with scope: own, the resolved entity declares ownershipField, and that value names a field present in that entity's own fields[]. An ownershipField naming a field the entity does not declare is not a valid ownership relation.' Both conjuncts are required and this manifest meets only the first, so it is rejected — 'valid' in item 3 means RESOLVABLE, never merely well-formed. Note the words 'that entity's OWN fields[]': a field of the same name declared on a DIFFERENT entity satisfies nothing, which is item 4's no-substitution principle applied one level down, from the entity to the field. COVERAGE GAP, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: that sibling-entity variant is not exercised anywhere in this set. 'Widget' is the only entity here, so nothing could have substituted even if a validator wanted to; a case with a second entity that DOES declare a field named 'created_by' would be needed to prove the field lookup is scoped to the resolved entity, and no such fixture exists yet. This case is a SECOND join — ownershipField against entities[].fields[].name — and although both operands sit inside one entity object, it still compares two instance values, which draft 2020-12 has no keyword for. The schema will and should ACCEPT this document; that accept is not a schema defect. OBSERVED AT THE VALIDATOR LAYER (packages/contracts/validation/app-manifest-relations.mjs, ADR 0009): rejected with AZ7_TARGET_OWNERSHIP_FIELD_UNDECLARED at /entities/0/ownershipField, which is a DIFFERENT code from the AZ7_TARGET_ENTITY_NOT_OWNED that az7-n3 and az7-n4 produce. That distinctness is itself the evidence: a validator checking only the first conjunct would ACCEPT this manifest, and one that rejected it as NOT_OWNED would be rejecting for a reason that is not true of it. Read the code, not just the verdict. PROVENANCE, KEPT DELIBERATELY: authored as an OPEN QUESTION with expectedOutcome UNDECIDED, because AZ7 as originally stated to QA said only that the entity must declare 'a valid ownershipField' and did not define 'valid'. Had the answer been 'well-formed is enough', this one-word change would have been a complete bypass of the CWE-863 fix and QA would have reported AZ7 as only partially closed. Item 3 settled it; the expectation was set from that recorded decision, not from observed behaviour, and it changes only if item 3 changes. STILL NOT DECIDED, AND NOT ASSUMED HERE: whether the ownership field must additionally be 'required: true' and of type 'reference'. A nullable owner column silently un-scopes every row where it is null, so QA recommends both, but no fixture in this set asserts it and this fixture's REJECT does not depend on it.
